This is a publication from the ISAAA (backed by the USDA/Monsanto/Bayer) listing worldwide genetically engineered crop production location and quantities. Genetically engineered foodstuffs are basically dead in the developed world outside of the United States. As you can see from their own data, in the industrial world there are about 80 million hectares of planted GMO crops. 71 million of those hectares are in the United States alone. Also note that the acreage of planted genetically engineered crops is decreasing in the developed world. Not their growth is decreasing but there's actually been a net decline year over year. This is the reason they're pushing so hard for genetic engineering in the undeveloped world.

They're also relying on angle shooting the definition of genetic engineering. Many places in the EU have partially or completely banned genetically engineered foodstuffs. And nearly everywhere requires labeling. However, the EU defines a genetically modified foodstuff as essentially being anything that occurs outside of natural recombination, like artificial selection. The catch is that Monsanto recently licensed CRISPR. CRISPR technology is based on a natural biological process which they're going to try to argue excludes CRISPR engineered foodstuffs from being considered genetically engineered foodstuffs. I think this angle shoot seems unlikely to hold in the EU.

Ultimately the article about the companies starting to limp is not entirely untrue. They're still behemoths, but outside of the US their future is very uncertain as far as foodstuffs go.
